messages.subject: Re: Change part of the Legend Order
parts:
Hi Jane,

Your example is complicated and not reproducible (at least I could not
load your dataframe.txt data). Please consider constructing a smaller
example that illustrates your problem, including readable data so we
can reproduce it.

Best,
Ista
On Wed, Feb 13, 2013 at 12:30 PM, Jane <janeco...@googlemail.com> wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> I have created the attached plot using ggplot2 and I'm really happy with it
> except that the colour and legend placing of the negative data are the
> reverse of what I want. The code I used to create the plot is below and the
> data frame is also attached.
>
> plot.data = data.frame(time)
>
> #add all Ox production reaction rates
> plot.data["CH3CO3 + NO = CH3O2 + NO2"] = data$"CH3CO3 + NO = CH3O2 + NO2" +
> data$"CH3O2 + NO = CH3O + NO2" + data$"Production Others" +
>
> data$"HO2 + NO = NO2 + OH"
> plot.data["CH3O2 + NO = CH3O + NO2"] = plot.data$"CH3CO3 + NO = CH3O2 + NO2"
> - data$"CH3CO3 + NO = CH3O2 + NO2"
> plot.data["Production Others"] = plot.data$"CH3O2 + NO = CH3O + NO2" -
> data$"CH3O2 + NO = CH3O + NO2"
> plot.data["HO2 + NO = NO2 + OH"] = plot.data$"Production Others" -
> data$"Production Others"
>
> #add all Ox consumption reaction rates
> plot.data["NO2 + O3 = NO3"] = data$"NO2 + O3 = NO3" + data$"HO2 + O3 = OH" +
> data$"O1D = OH + OH" + data$"Consumption Others" + data$"O3 = UNITY"
> plot.data["HO2 + O3 = OH"] = plot.data$"NO2 + O3 = NO3" - data$"NO2 + O3 =
> NO3"
> plot.data["O1D = OH + OH"] = plot.data$"HO2 + O3 = OH" - data$"HO2 + O3 =
> OH"
> plot.data["Consumption Others"] = plot.data$"O1D = OH + OH" - data$"O1D = OH
> + OH"
> plot.data["O3 Dry Deposition"] = plot.data$"Consumption Others" -
> data$"Consumption Others"
>
> #reshape data frame from wide to long for ggplot
> plot.data = reshape(data = plot.data[1:217,], idvar = names(plot.data)[1],
> times = names(plot.data)[-1], timevar = "reaction", varying =
> list(names(plot.data)[-1]), v.names = "rate",
> direction = "long")
>
> #add factor to control where plot layer is placed
> plot.data$reaction = factor(plot.data$reaction, levels = c("CH3CO3 + NO =
> CH3O2 + NO2", "CH3O2 + NO = CH3O + NO2", "Production Others", "HO2 + NO =
> NO2 + OH",
> "NO2 + O3 =
> NO3", "HO2 + O3 = OH", "O1D = OH + OH", "Consumption Others", "O3 Dry
> Deposition"))
> #data plot
> png(file = "OXBudget_sum_of_reaction_rates.png", width = 900, height = 700,
> units = "px", type = "cairo")
> plot = ggplot(plot.data, aes(x = time, y = rate, fill = reaction))
> plot = plot + geom_area(position = "identity", alpha = 0.8)
> plot = plot + geom_line()
> plot = plot + theme(legend.text = theme_text(size = 10))
> plot = plot + guides(fill=guide_legend(title="Reaction"))
> plot = plot + theme(strip.text.x = element_text(size = 10))
> plot = plot + xlab("Time (days)")
> plot = plot +
> ylab(expression(paste(Reaction~Rate~(molecules~cm^{-3}~s^{-1}))))
> plot = plot + opts(title="Odd Oxygen Family Budget: Sum of Reaction Rates
> Overlay without N2O5 Reactions")
> plot = plot + scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,3), breaks=seq(0, 3, 0.5))
> print(plot)
>
> Thanks,
> Jane
